title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
body: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals Scientists at the Allen Telescope Array have integrated the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to search for signals that may come from aliens — or the AI they built. October 30, 2026 by Chris Porter 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens. Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI. Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on. The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies. “As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear. Rather, it’s a breakthrough in translation.” Terabits a Second, Processed in Flight Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold. At the Allen Telescope Array, DAQIRI , a Holoscan platform library, enables the telescope to pull terabits per second of sensor data straight into GPU memory so observations are processed in flight rather than filling hard drives. CyberEther , a signal-processing framework developed at the SETI Institute, does the math using NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries including cuFFT and cuBLAS . Nexus , a web-based observatory orchestrator, acts as the agent harness. It gives agents a single source of truth for instrument state, compute resources and pipelines and lets researchers monitor packet loss, read live spectrograms and rewrite signal-processing blocks — all by prompting in natural language. The system can handle 2.4 terabits per second on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with inference running on premises, next to the instrument. Put together, the system enables an agent to steer a telescope’s antennae, calibrate and focus the instrument for a clean signal, catch and fix data errors and plot the result. Agents compress what would take humans weeks or years into hours. Science Fact, Not Fiction The pipeline has already proven itself, achieving the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar — a rapidly spinning stellar remnant that pulses like a cosmic lighthouse — in the Crab Nebula. Next, the team is evaluating open models including NVIDIA Nemotron for cases where data locality and turnaround matter most and for observatories that may someday run offline on the far side of the moon. Learn more about NVIDIA AI for science . title: Botox Fraud Doctor Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for $45M Medicare Scheme
body: Press Release Botox Fraud Doctor Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for $45M Medicare Scheme Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs California doctor Violetta Mailyan was sentenced yesterday to 15 years in prison for using her medical practice to fraudulently bill Medicare more than $45 million for Botox injection services that were medically unnecessary and never provided. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Violetta Mailyan, 45, of Glendale, California, owned and operated Healthy Way Medical Center, a clinic that purported to provide beauty and cosmetic services. Although Medicare reimburses medical providers for Botox injections when necessary to treat documented cases of chronic migraines, Mailyan billed and received payments for thousands of injections that were never provided, were provided only for cosmetic purposes, or were given to patients whose primary care physicians had not referred them for treatment of chronic migraines. Evidence also showed that Mailyan billed for thousands of injections, representing over $19 million, purportedly provided on days when her clinic was closed. Mailyan also billed for providing Botox injections when she was actually on vacation in Mexico, Hawaii, Las Vegas, Pennsylvania, and New York at various times throughout her fraud scheme. For example, Mailyan billed over $200,000 for purportedly providing Botox services to patients in California when she was actually relaxing on the beach in Cabo: Photograph from Mailyan’s Phone, Sent from Cabo, Mexico, the Same Day She Billed Medicare $34,560 For Services Purportedly Rendered in Glendale, California The evidence also showed that when Mailyan realized federal investigators were closing in, she tried to hide her tracks by falsifying medical records and forging Medicare beneficiary signatures, including for a man who was in federal prison during the time Mailyan claimed to have provided treatment. Mailyan submitted these records to federal investigators, intending to throw them off her trail and make it appear as though she had seen patients she had not actually seen. Mailyan used the money she stole to purchase luxury goods, including a $12,000 17th century crossbow and a $3,000 painting, depicted below: 17th Century Crossbow and $3,000 Painting that Mailyan Purchased with Medicare Fraud Proceeds In sentencing Mailyan, the Court commented that Mailyan’s fraud “was truly breathtaking in scope and shocking in its duration,” and that her actions were “almost unbelievable in their brazenness.” In addition to the prison sentence, the Court ordered the immediate forfeiture of over $16,029,742 worth of property seized from Mailyan, including real property, personal property, securities, and bank funds, effectively returning this taxpayer money to the United States. Mailyan was also ordered to pay $32,904,049.41 in restitution to Medicare, and the United States will vigorously pursue the return of these stolen funds. After a six-day jury trial ending in May 2026, Mailyan was convicted of nine counts of wire fraud and three counts of obstruction of a criminal investigation of a health care offense. The jury also found that Mailyan used the fraud proceeds to purchase two Tesla vehicles, including a Cybertruck, and five pieces of California real estate. HHS-OIG and FBI investigated the case. Trial Attorneys Sandor Callahan and Jeffrey A. Crapko of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section prosecuted the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Tara Vavere for the Central District of California’s Asset Forfeiture and Recovery Section is handling asset forfeiture matters. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1304
retained_feed_body: California doctor Violetta Mailyan was sentenced yesterday to 15 years in prison for using her medical practice to fraudulently bill Medicare more than $45 million for Botox injection services that were medically unnecessary and never provided.

title: Homeland Security Task Force:  Two Connecticut Men Found with 21 Kilos of Cocaine Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison
body: Press Release Homeland Security Task Force:  Two Connecticut Men Found with 21 Kilos of Cocaine Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, today announced that REGINALD ROGERS 38, of Woodbridge, and LESTER ARRINGTON, 34, of Naugatuck, have each been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Stefan R. Underhill in Bridgeport to 120 months of imprisonment and five years of supervised release for trafficking cocaine.  Rogers was sentenced today and Arrington was sentenced on October 27. According to court documents and statements made in court, as part of a Homeland Security Task Force investigation, on February 23, 2026, Connecticut State Police troopers stopped a 2024 Subaru Crosstrek in Trumbull.  Rogers was driving the vehicle and Arrington was a passenger.  A K9 sniff of the vehicle alerted for the presence of narcotics, and a subsequent search revealed approximately 21 kilograms of cocaine hidden in two compartments (“traps”) that were installed under each front seat.  Rogers and Arrington were arrested on state charges at that time. Rogers and Arrington each pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine.  Each is released on a $150,000 bond and they are required to report to prison on January 13. Arrington and Rogers agreed to the forfeiture of the vehicle. This investigation was led by the Drug Enforcement Administration with the assistance of the Bridgeport, Danbury, Stamford, and Stratford Police Departments.  The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Justyn P. Stokely and Lauren C. Clark. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion.  The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad.  Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement toward identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders.  In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Haven comprises agents and officers from the FBI, DEA, HSI, ATF, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation, U.S. Department of Transportation – Office of Inspector General, U.S. Department of Labor – Office of Inspector General, U.S. Department of Commerce – Bureau of Industry and Security’s Office of Export Enforcement, and Connecticut State Police, with prosecutions led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Connecticut. title: Fifth Alien Charged for Illegally Voting in Nevada
body: Press Release Fifth Alien Charged for Illegally Voting in Nevada Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – An Argentine national was charged today for illegally voting in the 2024 general election in Clark County, Nevada. “As this additional case demonstrates, there is a catastrophic failure to protect the ballot box,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “Every single illegal vote directly questions the very security of our elections and compromises public trust in our democratic processes. Our will enforce a zero-tolerance policy, and every single 611 case will be prosecuted to the absolute fullest extent of the law. We will aggressively hunt down and dismantle any attempts to compromise this election, and we will ensure that the voice of every lawful American citizen is completely protected from being diluted, neutralized, or stolen by illegal votes.” “Federal election laws are clear, and efforts to circumvent them will be investigated,” said Erin Burke, Special Agent in Charge for HSI Los Angeles. “HSI and our FBI partners will continue to identify and investigate alleged violations of federal election law, protect the integrity of the electoral process and ensure that those accused of criminal conduct are held accountable through the judicial process.” According to the criminal information, on or about November 5, 2024, Mariela Delia Mendoza, an Argentine national and a lawful permanent resident of the United States living in Las Vegas, illegally voted in an election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of President, Vice President, Member of the Senate, and Member of the House of Representatives. She was not a United States citizen. Mendoza is charged with one count of voting by an alien. The maximum statutory penalty is one year of imprisonment, a fine of up to $100,000, or both. An initial appearance date has not yet been scheduled. The FBI and HSI investigated this case. In addition to Mendoza, this month, the U.S. Attorney’s Office has charged four individuals for illegally voting, bringing the total in Nevada to five federally charged for illegal voting. These charges reflect the Department of Justice’s commitment to protecting the integrity of federal elections and ensuring that only eligible U.S. citizens participate in them. Jullie Ann Sumalinog Moore, from the Philippines and a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien for allegedly illegally voting in the 2024 General Election. Moneir Elzobier Ali Yousif, from Sudan and a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien for allegedly illegally voting in the 2024 General Election. Khalida Safi, from Afghanistan and a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien for allegedly illegally voting the 2024 General Election. Mlebinge Riziki Ramadhani, from the Democratic Republic of Congo and lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien for allegedly illegally voted in the 2022 General Election. An information is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. ### Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Nevada

title: Justice Department Announces Final Rule Allowing Federal Firearms Licensees to Voluntarily Use NICS for Employee Background Checks
body: Press Release Justice Department Announces Final Rule Allowing Federal Firearms Licensees to Voluntarily Use NICS for Employee Background Checks Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs OAG Today, the Department of Justice announced a final rule authorizing Federal Firearms Licensees (FFLs) to voluntarily use the FBI's National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS) to conduct background checks on certain current and prospective employees. “Firearms dealers deserve the confidence of knowing their employees are right with the law,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “This common-sense change delivers quick and clear background checks for firearms dealers based on the latest FBI information. The Trump Administration will always protect the Second Amendment and the rights of law-abiding gun owners.” “Under the leadership of President Trump and Attorney General Blanche, this FBI will always protect the Second Amendment and the rights of law-abiding gun owners,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “This is a common-sense change that appropriately expedites and clarifies the background check process for firearms dealers, and I want to thank our partners for working with us to make it happen.” The final rule implements a provision of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act , which directed the Attorney General to issue these regulations. Participation is optional for FFLs and requires the written consent of the employee. Under the final rule, an FFL may submit Firearm Handler Background Checks (FHCs) of eligible employees. Eligible employees include firearm handlers, employees of licensed manufacturers who have access to unfinished firearm components or manufacturing tools, and independent contractors or agents whose employment duties for an FFL allow them access to firearms, ammunition, or their manufacturing components. Those listed as responsible persons of FFLs are not eligible employees because they already undergo background checks through the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. Until now, Department of Justice regulations prohibited FFLs from contacting NICS for any purpose other than a proposed firearm transfer. NICS will search the same databases it does for a firearm transfer: the NICS Indices, the National Crime Information Center, and the Interstate Identification Index. The FFL will receive a NICS Transaction Number and one of three responses: "Pass," "Pending," or "Did Not Pass." FFLs will not receive any of the subject’s underlying record information. A "Did Not Pass" response does not prohibit an FFL from employing the person in a position that does not involve access to firearms or ammunition. Generally, an FFL may conduct one FHC per eligible employee every 12 months, unless the FFL has reasonable cause to believe the employee has become subject to a potentially prohibiting event. The FBI will not charge a fee for these checks. A subject whose FHC received a "Did Not Pass" response may request the reason for the response and may appeal that response in the same manner and to the same extent as a person who is denied a firearm transfer. The final rule addresses applicable public comments received on the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking that was published in December 2024. The final rule takes effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives will issue separate guidance to FFLs on how to document FHCs. Updated October 30, 2026 Components Office of the Attorney General Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Press Release Number: 26-1303

title: Former Turkey Leg Hut owner sentenced for role in arson-for-hire scheme
body: Press Release Former Turkey Leg Hut owner sentenced for role in arson-for-hire scheme Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Texas HOUSTON – A Houston businessman has been ordered to federal prison for conspiring to commit arson of a commercial building. Lyndell Leroy Price, 44, pleaded guilty June 11. U.S. District Judge Sim Lake ordered Price to serve 105 months in federal prison to be immediately followed by three years of supervised release. In handing down the sentence, the court noted that Price directed the arson of Bar 5015 without any regard for the safety of those who live nearby or the damage the explosion and fire would have on neighboring businesses. Judge Lake stated Price’s lack of respect for the law warranted a high sentence as a measure of deterrence and to protect the community. As part of his plea, Price admitted he directed others to intentionally set fire to Bar 5015, a Houston business his former partner owned on Almeda Road in Houston. Shortly before the fire, court records show that the owner had declined Price’s offer to buy into the bar and refused to sell his interest in the Turkey Leg Hut, an establishment he co-owned with Price’s estranged wife. In the early morning hours of June 12, 2020, the conspirators bought gasoline and gas cans before going to an area near the business. Wearing face coverings and carrying gasoline-filled containers, they walked to Bar 5015, poured gasoline across the entrance ramp and deck, ignited it, and fled. The fire caused significant damage to the business and endangered nearby occupied homes, commercial properties, and the electrical grid. After the arson, a member of the conspiracy called Price to report that the mission was complete. The conspirators then received payment from Price for their roles in the crime. John Lee Price, 39, Armani Williams, 28, Miziah Shepherd, 28, and Javon Harris, 27, all of Houston, previously pleaded guilty to the same charge and will be sentenced at a later date. Lyndell will remain in custody pending transfer to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility to be determined in the near future. FBI – Houston; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; and Houston Fire Department Arson Bureau conducted the investigation with assistance of Houston Police Department, Texas Department of Public Safety, and Harris County Constable’s Office – Precinct 4. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sebastian A. Edwards and Keri Fuller prosecuted the case. Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - Texas, Southern

title: District of Arizona Responds to Allegations of Non-Citizen Voter Registration
body: Press Release District of Arizona Responds to Allegations of Non-Citizen Voter Registration Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona PHOENIX, Ariz. – Today, U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine announced that his office has opened a case into recent reporting about three non-profit organizations registering non-citizens to vote in Arizona. The United States Attorney’s Office has already referred the matter to the FBI for a thorough federal investigation. On Monday, Oct. 26, U.S. Attorney Courchaine also sent letters to the Maricopa County Recorder and Arizona Secretary of State, expressing concerns about the recent reporting and encouraging those offices to review voter registrations associated with the accused non-profit organizations. On the eve of an important midterm election, the District of Arizona reminds the public that voting is limited solely to U.S. citizens. If you are a non-citizen, you may not vote in Tuesday’s election, even if you have legal authority to be in the country on a visa or as a legal permanent resident. Further, knowingly causing another person to be registered to vote while knowing that person is not entitled to do so would violate federal law. title: Justice Department’s Statement on Its Investigation of Vistra’s Acquisition of Cogentrix
body: Press Release Justice Department’s Statement on Its Investigation of Vistra’s Acquisition of Cogentrix Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward, Jr. of the U.S. Department of Justice issued the following statement today in connection with the Antitrust Division’s investigation into the acquisition of Cogentrix Energy (Cogentrix) by Vistra Corp. (Vistra) (together, the “Parties”): “Electricity customers in Maine, New Hampshire, and across New England will benefit from continued competition to generate affordable electricity. As New Englanders turn on the heat for the coming winter season, it’s critical that consumers not bear the risks of higher electricity bills. The Division anticipates that Vistra’s divestitures will save consumers throughout New England tens of millions of dollars annually in electricity bills.” “The Division has developed sophisticated methods for reviewing electricity generation mergers; these tools benefit American consumers and businesses that depend on affordable power,” said Deputy Assistant Attorney General G. Charles Beller of the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division. “Given the importance of affordable electricity for consumers, the Division will continue to monitor electricity transactions and the electricity sector as a whole. The Division will not hesitate to take appropriate action to safeguard competition in electricity markets.” On Jan. 5, Vistra announced an agreement to acquire Cogentrix from Quantum Capital Group. Both firms are electricity generation companies that compete in wholesale electricity and electric capacity auctions run by Regional Transmission Organizations (RTOs) or Independent System Operators (ISOs). RTOs and ISOs are nonprofit organizations responsible for managing and operating electric power grids within specific regions of the United States. These organizations also rely on internal or external market monitors, who are responsible for overseeing and evaluating the electricity market’s performance. Vistra’s acquisition of Cogentrix combines overlapping electricity generation asset portfolios in three different RTO/ISOs: PJM Interconnection LLC (which covers portions of the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic); ISO New England Inc. (ISO-NE); and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas. As required by federal law, Vistra and Cogentrix filed an application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for approval of the transaction. During FERC’s review process, the Internal Market Monitor of ISO-NE submitted comments to FERC stating that Vistra’s acquisition of Cogentrix raised concerns about a potential reduction in competition that may enable the exercise of market power in ISO-NE. While the Parties’ FERC application was pending, Vistra unilaterally decided to sell its Casco Bay Energy facility (Casco Bay) in ISO-NE. FERC acknowledged that it “consider[ed]” Vistra’s unilateral decision and approved the transaction without conditions. Following FERC’s approval, the Division continued its investigation to assess whether Vistra would have the ability and incentive to withhold electricity from the ISO-NE market after acquiring Cogentrix, notwithstanding the Casco Bay facility divestiture. The Division conducted a thorough investigation, reviewing thousands of documents, performing sophisticated economic modeling, and conducting extensive interviews with industry participants. After evaluating this evidence, the Division remained concerned that the portfolio of electricity generation units that would be combined in ISO-NE may result in a substantial lessening of competition, even with the sale of the Casco Bay facility. The Division’s legal and economic analysis followed the framework for evaluating electricity mergers described in the Division’s 2025 settlement complaint and competitive impact statement regarding Constellation Energy Corp.’s acquisition of Calpine Corp. Vistra and Cogentrix then unilaterally decided to sell Cogentrix’s gas-fired combined-cycle power plant in Rumford, Maine, which would reduce the combined firm’s ability and incentive to withhold electricity and raise prices in ISO-NE. The Division will continue to monitor Vistra’s sale of the Rumford facility. In the interim period, Vistra and Cogentrix must continue to abide by all applicable FERC regulations. The Division emphasizes that the outcome of this investigation is limited to its facts. title: Byrd Gang Members  Sentenced to Life Imprisonment for 2017 Double Homicide Committed Outside Edna Karr High School Basketball Game
body: Press Release Byrd Gang Members  Sentenced to Life Imprisonment for 2017 Double Homicide Committed Outside Edna Karr High School Basketball Game Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS – U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle announced that TERRAN WILLIAMS, a/k/a “Funky” (“WILLIAMS,”) TYRONE BOVIA, a/k/a “Sixx” (“BOVIA, ”) and JAVONTA DOLEMAN, a/k/a “Dutt” (“DOLEMAN,”) all from New Orleans, were sentenced to life imprisonment by United States District Judge Jane Triche Milazzo. In April 2025, WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN were found guilty by a jury after a multi-week trial of various violations, including RICO conspiracy, drug trafficking conspiracy, firearms conspiracy and Violent Crime in Aid of Racketeering (VCAR) murder. “The sentences of life imprisonment for WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN ensures that these violent murderers and drug traffickers will spend the rest of their lives in federal prison,” stated U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. “These prosecutions and sentences are examples of the federal government’s dedication to bring individuals who wreak havoc on our community to justice.” All three defendants were members of the Byrd Gang, also known as M3, MagFischer, 315 and Piff Gang, which operated primarily out of the former Magnolia Housing Development, but additionally had ties to the Westbank.  Its members distributed drugs- heroin, fentanyl, crack cocaine and marijuana- daily, and always possessed firearms. WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN participated in numerous drug trafficking activities and violent crimes and acted as gunmen for the Byrd Gang. On January 31, 2017, Lawrence Williams, IV, and Wynston Jackson, a/k/a “Ghost,” were shot and killed by the three defendants shortly after leaving an Edna Karr High School basketball game.  Jackson was a member of the rival Ghost Gang, sometimes referred to as the Goonie Gang, while Williams was an associate of Jackson. When Williams and Jackson left the basketball game and sat in a car in front of the school, WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN approached the car with two rifles and a handgun and unloaded a torrent of bullets.  Jackson attempted to return fire with his nine-millimeter handgun but was shot and killed on the scene. Williams, who was also shot, later died at the hospital. TYRONE BOVIA was also convicted for his role in another shooting that he committed in May 2017 at an apartment complex, where another Ghost Gang member, resided and was the intended target. BOVIA’S companion and fellow Byrd Gang member, Terrence Augustine, was shot and killed during this incident by return fire.  Byrd Gang member, James Alexander, has additionally pled guilty to this shooting. During the trial, evidence was presented that showed a slew of back-and-forth retaliatory shootings between the Byrd Gang and the Ghost Gang, much of which was fueled by social media posts, rap music, and videos.  Numerous individuals from both gangs have been shot and killed, and many innocent bystanders have likewise been shot during these inner-city rivalries. During the investigation, dozens of firearms, most with large-capacity magazines, as well as hundreds of rounds of ammunition, have been recovered from Byrd Gang members, including from the three defendants. WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN faced a mandatory life sentence for the Edna Karr murders which were charged in Counts 4 and 6 of the Superseding Indictment and were sentenced accordingly. WILLIAMS, BOVIA and DOLEMAN were additionally sentenced to life imprisonment for Count 1 (RICO conspiracy), and to 240 months for Counts 2 (drug conspiracy) and 3 (firearm conspiracy). BOVIA was also sentenced to 120 months imprisonment for discharging a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and crime of violence, which was charged in Count 9. This sentence was imposed consecutively to all other sentences. U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle praised the work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, especially the New Orleans Gang Task Force, the New Orleans Police Department, Sulphur Police Department, Jefferson Parish Sheriff’s Office, Louisiana State Police, and the Jackson County Sheriff’s Office in investigating this matter.  Assistant United States Attorneys Elizabeth Privitera, David Haller and Sarah Dawkins are in charge of the prosecution. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . *      *      * Contact Shane M. Forty-two Alleged Gang Members and Associates Charged with Trafficking Fentanyl and Methamphetamine Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
body: Press Release Forty-two Alleged Gang Members and Associates Charged with Trafficking Fentanyl and Methamphetamine Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – Four federal grand jury indictments charge 42 alleged members and associates of various San Diego County street gangs, including an increasingly violent and sophisticated Poway gang called Varrio Hidden Hills, with distributing large amounts of methamphetamine and fentanyl. In a coordinated takedown on Wednesday and Thursday, hundreds of FBI agents, members of the North County Regional Gang Task Force and federal, state, and local law enforcement officials arrested 35 defendants and executed 10 search warrants on homes and vehicles in Poway, Lemon Grove, San Diego, National City, Chula Vista, Imperial Beach, El Cajon, Oceanside, Escondido, Vista, Temecula, Murrieta, Riverside, and Tulare. As of 2:30 p.m. today, seven defendants were still being sought. Authorities seized drugs, guns, ammunition and cash during the takedown and throughout the two-year investigation. FBI agents came under fire while serving an arrest warrant at 6:10 a.m. Wednesday at a home in Lemon Grove. After agents identified themselves pursuant to standard protocol, multiple shots were fired in their direction from inside the residence through the front door and front window. No one was hit, and FBI agents retreated to safety after briefly returning fire. Tactical law enforcement personnel responded, and the target of the arrest warrant was taken into custody after coming out of the residence. The shooting is under investigation. “These arrests strike at the heart of this violent, sophisticated, Mexican Mafia connected criminal gang,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon, “The dangers our agents faced is a troubling reminder of the threats gang members pose, but also, the courage of those who confront them. We are grateful every agent is going home to their loved ones.” “Cases like this are only possible because of the outstanding partnerships across our federal, state, and local law enforcement community,” said Special Agent in Charge Mark Remily of the FBI San Diego Field Office. “Working together, we dismantled a violent criminal operation led by an assessed gang leader with suspected cartel associations, responsible for moving dangerous narcotics into our neighborhoods. This investigation also showed the level of violence these groups are willing to use when our agents came under fire while working to protect this community. Through unwavering teamwork, we stopped a network driving deadly drugs and violence into our neighborhoods. We will continue to use every lawful tool available to stop those threatening the safety of the people we serve.” “San Diego continues to be safer because of the law enforcement partnerships we have in this region.  The deputies, analysts and Sheriff leadership assigned to the North County Gang Task Force contributed their dedication and talents to this very complex case involving dozens of defendants in an investigation that crossed borders and multiple jurisdictions,” said San Diego County Sheriff Kelly Martinez. “I commend all the agencies and investigative teams involved in this effort and I’m grateful to see these dangerous individuals facing criminal consequences for their actions.” “This operation highlights the strength of collaboration among local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies in combating violent crime, dismantling criminal organizations, and removing dangerous drugs from our communities,” said CHP Chief Brandon Shipwash. “As California’s state police, the CHP remains committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners, utilizing our statewide resources and investigative expertise to hold those responsible accountable and protect the communities we serve.” “We extend our sincere appreciation to our federal partners for their outstanding cooperation, coordination, and commitment throughout this operation and successful takedown,” said Oceanside Chief of Police Taurino Valdovinos. “This operation sends a clear message: criminal activity will not be tolerated in San Diego County, and we remain committed to working together to hold those who threaten our communities accountable.” The arrests arise out of an FBI investigation that was initiated in mid-2024 into the Varrio Hidden Hills criminal street gang and associated illegal activity in Poway - specifically a senior-ranking documented member of the gang, John Marquez, and his associates. The investigation quickly expanded to all of San Diego County and other parts of California due to the expansive and overlapping criminal networks. During the two-year investigation, FBI agents and task force members learned that Marquez was the alleged leader of an international drug-trafficking organization and was associated with the Mexican Mafia. Marquez allegedly organized a multi-tiered distribution scheme using other San Diego County gang members and associates as distributors. Marquez oversaw separate chains of supply, set pricing, and collected drug proceeds to take back to his sources of supply in Mexico, according to court documents. He travelled continuously to and from Mexico to meet with his cartel-linked sources of supply and facilitate the importation of narcotics into the United States. The Mexican Mafia, a.k.a. “La Eme,” is a U.S.-based prison gang that has immense control over Hispanic street gangs in Southern California, directing illegal activities from prisons and collecting a portion of the proceeds from drug trafficking, illegal gambling, and other crimes committed on the streets. In addition to control over U.S.-based street gangs, the Mexican Mafia has ties to foreign terrorist organization (FTO)-designated criminal networks, including the Sinaloa Cartel, Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generacion (CJNG), and Mara Salvatrucha 13 (MS-13). The investigation uncovered an extensive operation funneling various narcotics from drug trafficking networks based in Mexico across the border and into San Diego and surrounding communities for further distribution. According to court documents, many of the defendants have criminal records that include robberies, assaults, and other violent and dangerous conduct. The evidence also reflected that Marquez continually collected drug proceeds from his sub-distributors to send back to his sources of supply in Mexico. For example, in one series of communications with one of his primary sources of methamphetamine and fentanyl, Marquez advised that he was preparing to go down to Mexico to pick up fentanyl and stated, “I have to count some money and send it to Sinaloa.” Court documents said Marquez’s organization earned substantial profits; the evidence reflected that Marquez regularly supplied methamphetamine at a price of between $750-$900 per pound, in addition to his profits from dealing fentanyl – which he worked with others to import for a price of $12,500 to $13,000 per kilogram. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jill Streja and Shivanjali A. Sewak. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Diego comprises agents and officers from FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, DEA, ATF, U.S. Marshals, Department of Defense, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Naval Criminal Investigative Service, IRS Criminal Investigation, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Customs and Border Protection and Interpol, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California. High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas (HIDTA) program, created by Congress with the Anti-Drug Abuse Act of 1988, provides assistance to Federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies operating in areas determined to be critical drug-trafficking regions of the United States. This grant program is administered by the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP). There are currently 33 HIDTAs, and HIDTA-designated counties are located in 50 states, as well as in Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and the District of Columbia. retained_feed_body: SAN DIEGO – Four federal grand jury indictments charge 42 alleged members and associates of various San Diego County street gangs, including an increasingly violent and sophisticated Poway gang called Varrio Hidden Hills, with distributing large amounts of methamphetamine and fentanyl. In a coordinated takedown on Wednesday and Thursday, hundreds of FBI agents, members of the North County Regional Gang Task Force and federal, state, and local law enforcement officials arrested 35 defendants and executed 10 search warrants on homes and vehicles in Poway, Lemon Grove, San Diego, National City, Chula Vista, Imperial Beach, El Cajon, Oceanside, Escondido, Vista, Temecula, Murrieta, Riverside, and Tulare. As of 2:30 p.m. today, seven defendants were still being sought. Authorities seized drugs, guns, ammunition and cash during the takedown and throughout the two-year investigation.

title: Stamford Man Sentenced to Additional Prison Time for Distributing Crack Prior to Reporting to Prison
body: Press Release Stamford Man Sentenced to Additional Prison Time for Distributing Crack Prior to Reporting to Prison Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that DANNY TURKVAN, also known as “Smooth” 55, of Stamford, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Stefan R. Underhill in Bridgeport to an additional 14 months of imprisonment for distributing crack cocaine after he had been sentenced in another federal case and prior to reporting to prison. On August 13, 2025, Turkvan was sentenced in Hartford federal court to 46 months of imprisonment and three years of supervised release for his participation in a southwestern Connecticut narcotics trafficking conspiracy.  Turkvan, who was released on a $150,000 bond, was ordered to report to prison on October 16, 2025.  An investigation revealed that Turkvan continued to distribute narcotics after his August 2025 sentencing.  Stamford Police arrested Turkvan on state charges on October 11, 2025, and seized crack cocaine that he intended to distribute. Turkvan has been detained since his arrest.  On July 8, 2026, he pleaded guilty in federal court to possession with intent to distribute cocaine base (“crack”). This investigation was conducted by the Stamford Police Department and the Drug Enforcement Administration.  The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Patricia Stolfi Collins. title: Florida Pharmacist Sentenced to Over 7 Years in Prison for Massive Illegal Oxycodone Distribution Conspiracy
body: Press Release Florida Pharmacist Sentenced to Over 7 Years in Prison for Massive Illegal Oxycodone Distribution Conspiracy Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A Florida pharmacist and pharmacy owner was sentenced yesterday to 90 months in prison for her role in illegally dispensing over 300,000 oxycodone 30mg pills to pharmacy patrons who had no medical need for the drug. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Olushola Yusuf, 60, of Tampa, dispensed oxycodone to nearly all of her pharmacy customers. Yusuf charged customers approximately 10 times the typical cost of the drug and required payment from them in cash. In total, Yusuf dispensed at least 335,351 pills of oxycodone 30mg during the conspiracy. Oxycodone 30mg is the maximum strength available of the drug and is both sought after and potentially dangerous due to its potency. It is typically prescribed to seriously ill patients, such as those suffering from chronic cancer pain or traumatic injuries. Photograph of Cash Paid to Yusuf for Illegally Distributing Oxycodone from her Pharmacy Yusuf owned and operated two pharmacies, Boots LLC doing business as, Striderite (Boots) in Margate, and Chans Pharmacy Plus, Inc. (Chans) in Pembroke Pines. Yusuf distributed oxycodone 30mg pills through these pharmacies. Customers drove long distances to have Yusuf fill prescriptions that they could not get filled at any other pharmacy. Some customers paid as much as $1,300 a month in cash to Yusuf for the drugs. And some customers were drug dealers who picked up oxycodone pills purportedly on behalf of dozens of patients at a time who were not present. According to witnesses at trial, Yusuf kept the doors to her pharmacies locked during business hours, directing employees only to open the door for certain identified customers. Yusuf continued to dispense oxycodone in this way even after repeated warnings from her employees and the DEA about the dangers of her pharmacy operations. After a two-week trial in July 2026, the jury convicted Yusuf of conspiracy to illegally distribute drugs and five counts of illegal drug distribution. Yusuf’s co-defendant, Saman Gimenez, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to illegally distribute drugs and is scheduled be sentenced later this year. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida; Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Chief of Operations Matthew W. Allen; FBI Co-Deputy Director Christopher Raia; and Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett for the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG) made the announcement. DEA, FBI, and HHS-OIG investigated the case. Trial Attorney Angela Benoit of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Jacqueline DerOvanesian for the Southern District of Florida prosecuted the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/fraud/health-care-fraud-section . Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1306

title: Indian National Pleads Guilty to $227M Medicare Fraud
body: Press Release Indian National Pleads Guilty to $227M Medicare Fraud Friday, October 30, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs An Indian national pleaded guilty today to a $227 million Medicare fraud scheme in which hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries’ personally identifiable information was purchased from a company based in Pakistan and used to bill Medicare for COVID-19 test kits that were never provided. According to court documents and statements made in court, Syed Murtuza Kablazada, 36, an Indian national residing in Des Plaines, Illinois, engaged in a scheme to defraud the Medicare program by submitting false and fraudulent claims for over-the-counter COVID-19 test kits that were not requested by beneficiaries or provided to them. Over the course of six months, starting in January 2023, Kablazada and his co-schemers acquired three Chicago-area laboratories, Chicago Care, V Care, and Al-Ameer. Kablazada then paid approximately $11 million to a purported telemarketing company based in Pakistan to obtain personally identifiable information for hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries. Using those Medicare beneficiaries’ information, Kablazada caused the laboratories to submit $227 million in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare for test kits that he knew were never requested by or shipped to the Medicare beneficiaries, for which Medicare paid approximately $136 million. To conceal their involvement in this scheme, Kablazada and his co-schemers paid themselves through overseas money transfers and unlicensed money transmitters, and they used the proceeds in part to purchase luxury vehicles. As part of his plea agreement in this case, Kablazada agreed to forfeit over $46 million in fraud proceeds that law enforcement seized from ten bank accounts. Kablazada pleaded guilty to two counts of health care fraud. He is scheduled to be sentenced on a later date and faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; Special Agent in Charge Ryan Whalen of the FBI Chicago Field Office; and Special Agent in Charge Thomas Ethridge of the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) made the announcement. The FBI Chicago Field Office and HHS-OIG investigated the case. Deputy Chief Patrick Mott and Trial Attorney Claire Sobczak Pacelli of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section are prosecuting the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Andres Almendarez for the Northern District of Illinois assisted in investigating and prosecuting this case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . Updated October 30, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1302
